newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ c/a deficit grows to 4.6 pct of GDP at Sept 30.
newsitem.headline: NZ c/a deficit grows to 4.6 pct of GDP at Sept 30.

text.p: New Zealand's current account deficit widened to 4.6 percent of GDP at September 30 from 4.1 percent at June 30, Statistics New Zealand said on Monday.
The September percentage was the highest level since December 1987 when it was 5.1 percent.
Economists had forecast a deficit of $1.71 billion for the quarter and $3.71 billion annually but the actual figures were $2.17 billion for the quarter and $4.20 billion for the year.
The department said adjustment for seasonality showed a $122 million current account deterioration from June to September.
It said an improvement in the merchandise trade balance in the quarter was not enough to offset a continuing decline in the adjusted invisibles balance.
The improvement in merchandise trade reflected improving exports and slowing growth in imports.
SNZ said the invisibles balance deteriorated as a result of a slowdown in immigration and tourist numbers.

"September 1996 quarter estimates of the trend in the current account balance show a continuation of the long-term decline evident since 1993, but with signs of an easing in recent periods," Government Statistician Len Cook said.
